title: ynotes --json output
description: Versioned JSON output for ynotes read/write commands. Success carries data; failure carries error and type. Parse stdout regardless of exit code. Query/list count mode returns counts instead of bodies. See the payload definitions and CHANGELOG.md for compatibility.

successEnvelope.title: success envelope
successEnvelope.description: Carries a successful result. Emitted on a `0` exit by every command, and also by `delete` on a `1` exit when some requested ids were unresolved (see `deleteData`), so a success envelope does not by itself imply a `0` exit. The `data` shape depends on the subcommand; the envelope fields are uniform across all of them.

failureEnvelope.title: failure envelope
failureEnvelope.description: Emitted when the command itself failed: exit `2` for a usage error, exit `1` for an engine/io/render failure. The converse does not hold, a non-zero exit is not always a failure envelope: `delete` reports unresolved ids inside a *success* envelope and still exits `1` (see `deleteData`). The diagnostic that would otherwise go to stderr is in-band as `error`; `type` is a stable enum so a consumer can branch programmatically without regex on the message.

error.description: The diagnostic message, the same text that would otherwise appear on stderr.

type.description: Error class. `usage`: bad invocation / bad value (exit 2). `engine`: an engine-level failure (exit 1). `io`: a binary-side I/O failure (exit 1). `render`: serialisation failure (exit 1).

initData.title: init --json data
initData.description: Payload for `ynotes init --json`: the selected store path and whether this invocation created it. Re-running init repairs managed merge guards without changing `created` from false.

created.description: true when this invocation created the store; false when it reopened and repaired an existing store.

saveData.title: save --json data
saveData.description: Payload for `ynotes save --json`: the saved note's identity. The id is a content hash of (target, scope, bundle, review basis, body) with no timestamp, so it is deterministic across machines and a retried identical save is a no-op. Note: subsequent maintenance may rotate the id, use (target, scope, body) as the stable lineage when caching a reference.

range.description: The line range captured at save time. For a file-scoped note this spans the whole file (1..line_count).

created.description: true when this save created a new note; false when an identical note already existed (idempotent save).

store_created.description: true only when this save created the .ynotes store at the Git root.

neighbours.description: Other notes on this file, earliest stored region first. Use these to inspect near-duplicates not removed by identical-location superseding. Empty when no other notes exist. Ranges are stored anchors; query resolves current locations.

body_excerpt.description: The existing note's first body line, truncated, enough to recognise a restatement without pulling every body on the file into the payload.

queryData.title: query --json data
queryData.description: Notes returned by a file or range query. The notes array includes anchored and drifted matches plus all orphans for the file.

notes.description: Overlapping anchored or drifted notes followed by every orphaned note for the file, regardless of interval.

malformed.description: Unreadable records relevant to this file, including unindexed records whose target is unknown. Skipped from `notes` because they cannot be resolved, but surfaced so corruption is never hidden (invariant #4). Always present; empty when there is nothing to flag.

warnings.description: Non-fatal advisories about this query, for example, that the target file does not exist (almost always a typo). The command still exits 0; the warning is the in-band signal. Always present; empty array when there is nothing to flag.

listData.title: list --json data
listData.description: Payload for `ynotes list --json`: every note in the store with its current anchor status.

malformed.description: Records under notes/ that could not be read or parsed. Skipped from `notes` because they cannot be resolved, but surfaced so corruption is never hidden (invariant #4). A filtered inventory retains unknown-target records because excluding them would assume what cannot be read. Always present; empty when there is nothing to flag.

warnings.description: Non-fatal advisories, populated when a path filter (`list <file>` or `list <dir>`) matched nothing, distinguishing 'this filter is empty' from 'the store is empty'. With no filter, an empty `notes` array is self-explanatory and `warnings` stays empty. Always present.

updateData.title: update --json data
updateData.description: Payload for `ynotes update --json`: the refreshed note's identity, plus the id it supersedes. The new note re-anchors against the current file (same target+scope, range re-resolved through the anchor ladder), so the id changes whenever the body, the file, or the resolved range did.

id.description: The refreshed note's id (content-hashed over the new identity).

previous_id.description: The id of the note this one supersedes. Equal to `id` when the update was a no-op (identical body and unchanged anchor).

range.description: The line range the refreshed bundle was captured at, the note's current resolved location.

created.description: true when this update wrote a new record; false when an identical content hash already existed.

confirmData.title: confirm --json data
confirmData.description: Payload for `ynotes confirm --json`: the note whose body was explicitly reviewed against current code. Confirmation advances the independent review basis and is the only body-preserving operation that can clear stale context after an edit.

range.description: The current code region against which the note body was reviewed.

changed.description: true when advancing the review basis changed the note's content-addressed identity.

created.description: true when confirmation wrote a new note record.

deleteData.title: delete --json data
deleteData.description: Per-ID deletion outcomes, partitioned into deleted, deleted_unreadable, ambiguous, and not_found. All arrays are present. Nonempty ambiguous or not_found produces exit 1 despite success: true. An unreadable record purged by full ID is a successful deletion. Inspect the partitions to determine complete success.

requested.description: How many ids the caller passed.

deleted.description: Notes that were removed (or, under `dry_run`, would be).

body_excerpt.description: The first line of the body, truncated at 80 characters with `…`. Useful as a confirmation; not the whole body.

deleted_unreadable.description: Ids of corrupt records purged by exact id (or, under `dry_run`, that would be). A malformed record cannot be read to supply a target/scope/body, so only its id is reported. Removal requires the full 64-character id, a short prefix can never purge an unreadable record (there is no body to preview, and a prefix could otherwise catch a healthy note). An entry here is a success, not a partial failure: it does not flip the exit code.

ambiguous.description: Prefixes that matched more than one note. None of the candidates are deleted (we never silently delete multiple matches for a single requested id).

not_found.description: Prefixes that matched no note in the store.

dry_run.description: true when invoked with `--dry-run`, nothing was actually removed.

pruneData.title: prune --json data
pruneData.description: Payload for `ynotes prune --json`: orphaned notes that were removed (or, under `dry_run`, would be). Drifted notes are never touched, `reanchor` is for them.

pruned.description: One entry per orphan removed (or that would be removed).

last_known.description: The line range the orphan was anchored at the last time the resolver could locate it.

body_excerpt.description: First line of the body, truncated at 80 characters with `…`.

kept.description: How many non-orphaned notes remain in the store.

dry_run.description: true when invoked with `--dry-run`, nothing was actually removed.

reanchorData.title: reanchor --json data
reanchorData.description: Payload for `ynotes reanchor --json`. Reports every note whose selectors were refreshed in place (`changed`), every note moved to a renamed file (`relocated`), every note deliberately left untouched with the reason (`skipped`), every already-anchored note whose body is still unreviewed (`review_pending`), and how many were already current (`unchanged`). Any note that moved gets a new id (the id hashes over target+bundle), `old_id`/`new_id` carry both for lineage tracking. Under `--dry-run` the same shape is emitted with `dry_run: true` and no writes occur.

dry_run.description: true when invoked with `--dry-run`, nothing was actually written.

changed.description: Notes refreshed in place (or that would be), the region moved or was edited within the same file. Each entry's `from` is the prior captured range; `to` is the range the refresher resolved to in the current file. A note that moved to a *different* file is reported under `relocated`, not here.

review_required.description: true when current code differs from the note's last explicit review basis. Reanchor refreshed location only; verify the body, then confirm it.

relocated.description: Notes relocated through a content-corroborated Git rename, or proposed relocations in a dry run. A changed target produces a new ID. If the region cannot be located at the destination, it is skipped instead. Always present.

from_target.description: The path the note was filed under before the rename.

to_target.description: The path it now lives at (the file's current name).

from.description: Where the region sat in the old file at save time.

to.description: Where it resolved to in the renamed file.

review_required.description: true when current code differs from the note's last explicit review basis.

skipped.description: Notes deliberately left untouched, with the reason. `reason_code` is the stable enum to branch on; `reason` is the human form.

reason_code.description: orphaned: the region cannot be identified. missing-target: the target is absent. symlink-escape: the target resolves outside the work tree. other: an unenumerated reason.

reason.description: Free-form human explanation suitable for display.

review_pending.description: Notes with current selectors whose code still differs from their review basis. They remain drifted and are also counted in unchanged. Verify the body before confirming with the reported current ID. Always present.

unchanged.description: Number of notes requiring no selector update, including review_pending entries.

filesData.title: files --json data
filesData.description: Annotated paths and counts, ordered by descending count then path. Existing targets need records and path checks; missing targets use content-corroborated Git rename detection. Unlocatable notes retain historical paths. Read-only. Ranges and statuses are omitted because not every note is resolved; use query or list for those.

files.description: Annotated files, most-annotated first. Empty on a store with no notes.

notes.description: How many notes are stored against this file.

total.description: Total notes across every file, the sum of `files[].notes`.

malformed.description: How many records under `notes/` could not be read or parsed. A count, not a list: `doctor` and `reindex` report the specifics.

reindexData.title: reindex --json data
reindexData.description: Payload for `ynotes reindex --json`. The index (`by-path.json`) is a cache rebuilt from the note records on disk, which are the source of truth; this reports how the rebuilt index differed from the one that was there. A healthy store yields empty `recovered`/`dangling`/`malformed`. Under `--dry-run` the same shape is emitted with `dry_run: true` and the on-disk index is left untouched. Reindex never invokes the anchor ladder, so note ids are unaffected.

dry_run.description: true when invoked with `--dry-run`, the on-disk index was not written.

scanned.description: Note records read successfully while walking `notes/`.

indexed.description: Distinct notes in the rebuilt index.

recovered.description: Ids found on disk that the previous index did not list, pointers that were missing and have been restored. Always present; empty when the index already agreed with disk.

dangling.description: Ids the previous index listed with no file behind them on disk, dangling pointers that have been dropped. Always present; empty when none.

malformed.description: Paths of unreadable or malformed records excluded from the rebuilt index. Their files are left untouched. Always present.

git.description: The `git` binary's version, or null when no `git` is on PATH (the git-transport rung is then disabled).

store.description: The discovered `.ynotes` store: the string "none" when no store was found, otherwise a single-key object.

path.description: The `.ynotes` directory, present when a store was located but its notes could not be read; absent when store discovery itself failed (no valid `.ynotes` was located), in which case the implicated path is carried in `reason` instead.

reason.description: Why the store (or its notes) could not be read; carries the implicated path inline when the discrete `path` field is absent.

health.title: store health
health.description: Read-only health, present only for a discovered store. Healthy means index.status is healthy, recovered and dangling are zero, and malformed and gitattributes_missing are empty.

malformed.description: Unreadable or malformed record paths. Inspect them before repair or exact-ID deletion. Reindex repairs the cache, not record contents. Always present.

gitattributes_missing.description: Missing managed merge-guard lines. Store writes attempt best-effort restoration. Rerun doctor to verify repair, or fix the file manually if it remains unwritable. Always present.

lookupData.title: lookup --json data
lookupData.description: Payload for `ynotes lookup --json`: the notes matching a stable (target, body) handle, each with its current id and anchor status. Use this to re-derive a note's live id, which rotates on reanchor/update.

notes.description: Every note matching the lookup filters, in list order. Empty when nothing matched (exit 0).

storeAbsent.title: Store absent
storeAbsent.description: Successful absent-store result for CLI files and MCP files, recall, notes, or reanchor. Does not create a store.

querySpec.title: query request echo
querySpec.description: The request `query --json` echoes back: the file and location arguments exactly as passed. Shared by the full and `--count` query payloads.

file.description: The file argument as passed on the command line.

at.description: The location argument: `LINE`, `START:END`, or empty for a whole-file query.

countBreakdown.title: status breakdown
countBreakdown.description: A tally of resolved notes by anchor status, emitted by `--count` summary mode in place of the note bodies. `total` equals `anchored + drifted + orphaned`.

orphaned.description: Notes no content rung could locate.

queryCountData.title: query --count --json data
queryCountData.description: Status counts for a query, using the same rename-aware resolution as the full read. Carries count instead of notes and a malformed count instead of record details.

malformed.description: How many relevant records could not be read or parsed, the count-mode analogue of `queryData.malformed[]`, so corruption is still flagged in summary mode (invariant #4). Pull the full query payload for record paths and any recoverable ids.

warnings.description: Non-fatal advisories, as in the full `query` payload. Always present; empty when there is nothing to flag.

listCountData.title: list --count --json data
listCountData.description: Payload for `ynotes list --count --json`: the status breakdown across the listed set in place of the notes. Distinguished from `listData` by carrying `count` (not `notes`); `malformed` here is a count, not an array.

malformed.description: How many records under notes/ could not be read or parsed, the count-mode analogue of `listData.malformed[]` (invariant #4).

warnings.description: Non-fatal advisories, populated when a path filter matched nothing. Always present; empty when there is nothing to flag.

showData.title: show --json data
showData.description: One note selected by ID or unambiguous prefix, resolved against current code with the same rename corroboration as query and list.

warnings.description: Non-fatal advisories, populated, for example, when the note's target file does not exist on disk (the note then resolves `orphaned`). Always present; empty when there is nothing to flag.

note.title: Resolved note
note.description: A stored note resolved against the current file.

status.description: anchored: region located and intact against its review basis, possibly at a new position. drifted: located, but its content differs from its review basis. orphaned: could not be identified. None of these statuses establishes that the note's claims are true.

stale.description: Agent convenience: false only for an anchored note; true for drifted or orphaned. A pure function of status, provided so an agent can branch on one boolean.

resolved_range.description: Where the note resolved to in the current file, or null for an orphan.

previous_range.description: Present when the region is no longer at its saved range: on an anchored or drifted note that moved, and on an orphaned note (its last known range). Absent when the note resolves where it was saved.

relocated_from.description: Present when a note resolves through a file rename but is still stored under its pre-rename target. Pair with `relocated_to` for both sides of the pending migration; `reanchor` makes it durable.

relocated_to.description: Present with `relocated_from`: the current path where the note's region was content-corroborated. This lets `list`, `query`, and MCP inventories surface a pending rename without writing.

rungs.description: Present only with --explain: each selector-ladder rung's outcome (the agreement vector).

rung.title: Rung outcome
rung.description: One matching method's evidence. Scores are method-specific diagnostics in [0, 100], not a combined confidence. See ynotes skills get core --full for the scoring reference.
Which rung: git transport (R1), exact quote (R2), fuzzy alignment (R3), tree-sitter structure (R4), saved position (R5).

result.description: hit: located the region. miss: ran but found nothing. skipped: could not run (e.g. not a git repo) and is not held against the result.

range.description: Present only on a hit: where this rung believes the region now is.

score.description: Present only on a hit: the rung's own confidence in its range. Scale per rung, git: 100 unchanged / 90 moved-untouched / 70 moved-touched; quote: 95 exact text still at the saved position / 90 disambiguated by prefix-suffix context, or unique at capture and still unique / 55 ambiguous or unverified; structural: 55–95 (95 = identical fingerprint); fuzzy: 45–80 (capped below 90, fuzzy alone never anchors); position: 20 in-range / 10 clamped (diagnostic only, never consulted by the verdict).

indexHealth.title: index cache health
indexHealth.description: Readability and identity drift of the rebuildable by-path cache observed while serving a read. Reads report this state but never repair it.

status.description: Whether the index parsed successfully, was absent, or was malformed.

recovered.description: Record ids present on disk but absent from the index.

dangling.description: Index ids with no record file behind them.

malformedNote.title: Malformed note record
malformedNote.description: A record under notes/ that could not be read or parsed as a note. Surfaced by read paths even when it is absent from the index, so corruption is never hidden (invariant #4).

id.description: The id encoded by a canonical record path, or null for an irregular filename.

target.description: The cached target, or null when an unindexed malformed record has no readable source for it.

path.description: Store-relative path to the unreadable record.

error.description: Why the record could not be read or parsed. Free-form, for display, branch on an entry being present, not on this text.

noteId.description: Content-addressed note id: the SHA-256, hex-encoded, of (target, scope, bundle, review basis, body). Deterministic, no timestamp or randomness. **Rotates on reanchor, update, and confirm** when one of those hash inputs changes. To cache a stable handle to a note across maintenance, use the (target, scope, body) tuple rather than the id.

target.description: The note's target file, relative to the store's work tree, with forward slashes.

scope.description: A contiguous line range or the whole file. A single-line note uses range with equal endpoints. The stored scope retains its original variant for ID compatibility.

schemaVersion.description: Contract version. Field changes require a version bump; consumers should reject unrecognised versions. See CHANGELOG.md for compatibility changes.
